message.content: In Christian theology, Jesus Christ is regarded as the central and most pivotal figure—often described as the fulfillment of the Old‑Testament prophets and the ultimate revelation of God’s plan.  While Jesus is seen as the culmination of prophetic tradition, many Christians also honor earlier prophets such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others for their foundational role in shaping the narrative that leads to the New Testament.  Thus, while Jesus is considered the most important figure in Christianity, the prophets of the Hebrew Scriptures are also highly respected and integral to Christian belief.
